I also lie awake staring at the ceiling only to wake up exhausted at 4 AM, and my body feels like it's moving through molasses while my brain is too foggy to even read a single line of a book.\n\nDoctor: Have these symptoms been causing major problems in your daily life, like at work, with self-care, or in your relationships? Also, do you feel hopeless or have thoughts that life is not worth living?\n\nPatient: Yes, they've caused real problems—I've been calling out sick more, letting my library cataloging pile up, and my supervisor even pulled me aside about my slipping performance. However, I don't feel hopeless, and I definitely haven't had any thoughts of life not being worth living.\n\nDoctor: Did these symptoms start within a few months of the separation, and have they been steadily present since then without long periods of feeling back to normal?\n\nPatient: Yes, they started right when the separation became official and I moved into my own apartment about three months ago. Since there wasn't a major life crisis like a separation back then, I usually just chalked those dragging lows up to work stress or my own personality.\n\nDoctor: Have you ever had a time before this separation when you felt depressed or lost interest in things for at least two weeks, even when there was no major stressor happening?\n\nPatient: Yes, those low periods would absolutely last for several weeks at a time, sometimes even longer, where I just wanted to isolate myself.
